videos.title_guess: Carrier Spotlight: Nassau's Athos Annuity (launch event; transcript title says 'Zaghorn's' – likely caption artifact for Nassau)
videos.summary: Launch/training event for Nassau Athos, a fixed index annuity (FIA) built by Genesis Development Group (inventors of the index annuity, 1995) and distributed via Elevation, exclusive-ish to Annuity.com among large IMOs. Brett Blake frames the accumulation market opportunity; Steve (Elevation, ex-Annexus original 12) and Chad Onstad (Genesis chief growth officer) with Ryan Whitty explain volatility targeting, par vs cap data from 30+ years of back-casting, and the product's 'extendable point-to-point' design: annual reset that can be extended yearly, par rate rising on each extension and applied retroactively, 90% protected-value stop loss, daily value tracking/full daily value at death, and 'Dial-a-Bonus' blended bonus/non-bonus. Covers service, compliance/replacement rules, carrier rating (AM Best B++), competition vs RILAs, and how agents get support (Talon).

terms_definitions.definition: The amount a carrier can spend on index options for the client (e.g. ~4%), funded by the yield on the bond portfolio backing the contract; carriers control it but not option prices.
Percentage of index gain credited to the client; set by option budget ÷ option price. Doubling option cost halves par; presenters say it should move inversely to option cost.
Maximum index return credited per period. Presenters claim par beats cap ~80% of time historically.

Index overlay that flattens option cost so renewal rates stay stable; ~15% target ≈ average S&P realized volatility, delivering ~100% of the index on average; a 5% target yields only ~1/3 of the market.

Athos's patent-pending design: annual point-to-point that, on anniversary (+15 days), client can reset (lock gains) or extend another year; each extension raises par rate and applies it retroactively to all gains in the term.
On each extension 90% of the daily account value becomes a floor that can't be lost; principal itself never at risk.
Client can see value daily; full daily value (not last anniversary value) paid at death; surrender at daily value within 15 days after anniversary.

Splits a premium between bonus and non-bonus Athos policies so only the bonus needed to cover surrender-charge breakeven is used, leaving higher blended par (example: 45% par bonus-only vs 58% blended).
If client dies before the credit date, the gain for that year is zero — like not passing Go.
Presenters' term for carriers starting with a subsidized high cap then cutting at renewal.
Registered index-linked annuity; buffer strategies put principal at risk; presenters position Athos as RILA-like upside with 100% principal protection.
Checkbox on the application so extension happens automatically each anniversary; can be undone at any anniversary; recommended by Steve.

claims_stats.claim: Annuity.com CEO: estimated ~$49 trillion in retirement income money, some estimates $400T in a decade; accumulation opportunity ~10x the guaranteed income opportunity; $2–4T re-homed yearly from IRAs/401(k)s, ~54% seeking guaranteed income.
Genesis: created original index annuity in 1995; 17 patents, ~10 pending; tracking 32 years of back-test data.

Back-casting claims: par outperforms cap ~80% of time; 2-year par beats 1-year par 84% (90% dynamic); 1-year cap vs 2-year par: cap loses 90–92.5%; S&P positive 78% of last 50 years, 77 of 78 double-digit [as stated].

Vol-target index: last 10 years lagged S&P by 23 bps, captured ~98% of S&P par rate and ~80% of Nasdaq par; 20-yr average 'S&P 103% vs vol index ~120%'; v2 index added ~16% extra over time vs v1 (presenter claim).
Illustration: $100k annual reset → 269 vs extendable 371 (25–40% more efficient); 7-yr hypothetical with 90% protected value 263 vs daily value 292 / 254 after crash.
Par rates started at 70% (S&P TCA) and 60% (Nasdaq); Friday rate increase announced: Nasdaq to 65%, TCA to 75%.
Cap version starts ~9% (back-test high 17.75%); bonus cap version peak 12.25%; cap does not apply retroactively.
Early renewal data: 19% of extended policies renewed at 52–59% par; 81% at 60–61% from 48% start with 12% bonus; cap policies renewed 5%→7.75% (55% increase).
Dial-a-bonus example: $500k, 16% bonus → blended 8% effective bonus; par 45%→58%; 10-yr value 133k→153k per illustration.
10-year surrender, 7% free withdrawal after year 1; no fees or spreads; par version has no cap (a separate cap version exists); approved everywhere but NY and ME.
Compliance: replacement of contracts 2+ years old approved in 24–48 hours if bonus makes client breakeven or better; liquidity: 6 months if age ≤64, 12 months if 65+; VAs 1 year+ often OK.
Premium range: $15,000 minimum, $2.5M max (up to $5M with a call).
Agent street comp: 100 bps special from now through end of November (as stated).
Service: 22-second average phone answer, US call center, 4.9 Trustpilot (10,500+ reviews); presenters cite competitors 1.3–2.2 on Trustpilot.
Athos exclusive-ish: not available via Simplicity, Integrity (or their shops); built 'for truly independent' agents; Annuity.com agents appointed via Annuity.com SureLC, not ECA.
Athos has highest apps per producer among Nassau platform products (presenter claim); goal: 3 cases to 'click'.
1-year TCA return cited as underperforming S&P due to choppy tariff/Iran-conflict market (presenter's explanation).

sales_teachings.teaching: Sell it as an annual reset
sales_teachings.detail: Plain-English pitch: 'It's an annual reset. At year-end we can take the gains or reinvest the gains for more rate; you decide by anniversary + 15 days.'

sales_teachings.teaching: Use only as much bonus as needed
sales_teachings.detail: Bonuses come out of the option budget; dial bonus to breakeven on surrender charges rather than as incentive; 20% bonus on 4% budget over 10 years ≈ halves option budget.
Point-to-point pays zero on death before credit date (364/365 chance); explain the 'artificially inflated cap' concept and why daily value at death matters.
RILA buffers risk principal near retirement (sequence risk); Athos offers RILA-like upside with 100% principal protection.
Protected value reduces sequence-of-return risk; presenters see 4–5% withdrawals as comfortable.
Check box at application; easier to unwind at a good anniversary than to resell each year.
Up to two buckets per index; extend/reset buckets independently; switching index resets to base par; avoid fixed account in an FIA.
Target 2+-year-old bonus contracts, VAs, income riders ('fake money').
Heartburn came from low 5% targets, bond exposure, and bespoke multi-asset algorithms; Athos uses plain S&P/Nasdaq or cash.

notable_quotes.quote: The guys that invented annual reset and the name annual reset are right here.
We didn't build a new index. We built a better way to squeeze the juice out of the return.
It's not where we start. It is where we finish.
If I give you a bonus, it's not free money, it's coming out of the option budget that they could have otherwise given to you.
Just cuz they say it's guaranteed doesn't mean that it's guaranteed. ... You got to read the contract.
We give you RILA-like performance now with 100% principal protection.
The goal is three cases... First one, you're kind of excited... the second one, you're like, okay, what did I do? And the third one, click.
I think that the opportunity for agents to participate in accumulation is 10 times larger than the opportunity that we have with guaranteed income.
We built this to be for the truly independent people.

terms_definitions.definition: Annuity.com pays agents the full commission carriers intended; described as non-negotiable and no split with the IMO.

Annual bonus program: over first $5M production the company shares overrides as incentives (team building, stock); above $5M the company's earnings on that agent are capped and all company dollars pass through to the agent.
Residual override program: 50% of company overrides fund overrides on recruited agents' production up to seven levels deep, as long as both remain with Annuity.com.
Letter given before first case allowing agent to leave and write elsewhere; few use it.
New agent pairs with experienced agent; commission split 20% each for appointment setting, fact finding, case design, presentation, close; experienced agent may earn up to 80%.

Free enrollment + move one carrier's contracts; pre-release letter lowers risk.
'Rather earn 1% off 100 people's efforts than 100% of my own' – framing for Agency Builder.
Offer to run individual comp math; follow-up meeting after call covers compensation.

Agents are independent, but they're really not free.
They're not here to serve us. It's your business and we want to be able to support you in that.
We're not going to take money out of their pockets to line our pockets.
I'd rather earn 1% off 100 people's efforts than 100% of my own efforts.

'I'm seeing many of my clients' premiums increase as they age because they haven't given enough thought to how they receive retirement income... I've brought in a retirement income specialist... free service... would you like to schedule time with her?'

sales_teachings.teaching: Goal is confidence not just a sale
sales_teachings.detail: Clients with pensions may not need an annuity yet still benefit.
Say at end of Medicare call you'll review their case and call back; schedule 10-minute follow-up to connect with specialist; can double income during AEP.
Start with 20% appointment-setting; add steps as comfortable; specialists hop in anytime.

notable_quotes.quote: It takes one client who you're able to help. And the cost to do that is zero to you.
You observe, you learn, and you earn.
The goal is to bring confidence to your clients, not necessarily just to sell an annuity, but we hope we sell an annuity on the way.
We pay 100% of our street commission to our agents. There's no funny money here.
Is that worth a phone call?
It just requires having the courage to make the phone call.
We have an epidemic of fear when it comes to retirement finances.
Pick up the phone and dial one client who trusts you.

videos.title_guess: CORE & AgentPay Live Walkthrough (beta launch, ~late June/early July 2026)
videos.summary: Live demo by Bruce (Annuity.com leadership) with developer Alan of CORE (Carriers, Opportunities, Resources, Earnings), the new custom-built agent dashboard at commission.annuity.com, and AgentPay/e-wallet (via TygaPay [spelling unclear]) with a tax-saving marketing wallet. Covers dashboard (production, company-dollar progress toward $1M/$3M/$5M, FLP counts for team levels), orders/cases, downline, customers, earnings drill-down, chargebacks, e-wallet setup and $1.50 withdrawal fee, beta feedback buttons, and Q&A on support threads, visibility, anniversary dates, and real-time vs final numbers. Brett closes with the strategy.

claims_stats.claim: CORE is live (beta) with real imported orders; imports may show discrepancies; real-time updates but numbers finalize after month close.
Log in at commission.annuity.com (singular); login seamless across systems.
Dashboard shows personal production and company-dollar progress toward $1M/$3M/$5M; recent orders, paid/in-good-order status; FLP progress to next tier; downline hierarchy; customer list.
Earnings drill-down: month → bonus category → agent → policies/carriers; no customer data shown to other agents.
Orders entered through Firelight flow in automatically; others are found from carrier and entered by Annuity.com operations.
Built-in support email per order; threads reply-all and integrate with system; same view for internal team.
E-wallet: commission payments via AgentPay start first Monday after July 4; replaces Mercury; all agents must register new banking; auto-withdraw option.
Each transfer to bank costs $1.50 (ACH).
Marketing wallet example: $10,000 commission, move $2,000 → 1099 shows $8,000; funds restricted to approved marketing expenses; Brett frames it as buying marketing credits.
Chargebacks show in red and draw down future street commission/overrides; Rebel 1 charges back first-year distributions.
Premium additions treated as new policy on addition date.
Prior attempt (as president of another company) cost >$4M, nine developers, almost a year, never launched; current team smaller and custom.
Previously third-party tools meant slow bids/turnaround; custom development enables fast iteration.
Plans: maturity alerts for MYGAs, aggregated carrier commission visibility, integration with Lead Pro and Agent IQ; LOA (letter of authorization) structure under consideration.

synthesis: PLATFORM (company facts): Annuity.com's tech stack across these videos: Agent HQ (portal; new left-nav, mobile/tablet friendly, profile feeds AI-optimized 'find an agent' and personal annuity.com subdomain sites), Agent IQ (AI engine at agent.annuity.com; AI case-planning upgrade coming), CORE (commission.annuity.com beta: dashboard of production, company-dollar progress to $1M/$3M/$5M stock tiers and $5M cap, FLP-based team tiers, orders/cases with embedded support email, downline, earnings drill-down, chargebacks, anniversary-day tracking; real-time but finalize after month close; free to all agents; Firelight orders flow automatically), AgentPay (e-wallet with TygaPay [unclear] replacing Mercury; $1.50 per bank transfer; marketing wallet reduces 1099 via prepaid approved marketing spend), Lead Pro ($199/mo CRM/newsletter/subdomain/phone/directory/Hegna bundle), cases@annuity.com and athos@annuity.com multi-bid email, Guaranteed Income Comparison chart, weekly tech call (Austin Openshaw), SureLC link for Annuity.com. RAMP: began as Reducing Annual Medicare Penalties; Fall 2026 goal $1,000 in 30–45 days via a single referral to a retirement income specialist; 20% appointment share (e.g. $1,500 on $150k case at 5%); later evolved to a 'retirement income review' script with a 15–20 min first meeting and a results meeting a week later. COMPENSATION: 100% street, Cap the Company over $5M, Agency Builder up to 7 levels funded by 50% of overrides, stock ($1k/$4k/$10k at $1M/$3M/$5M), pre-release letter, team selling 20% splits. Narrative: agent-first, ownership, transparency, technology reducing admin, truly independent (exclusive products not available to Simplicity/Integrity/AmeriLife groups). EDUCATIONAL: Athos (extendable point-to-point, par>cap data, vol control, dial-a-bonus) is a carrier/product training; Bill Broach's tips (fact-finder-centered selling, third-party influence, barber mindset, permission language) and RAMP referral scripts are sales education. CAUTIONS: many performance figures are presenters' back-tests/claims, not verified; caption artifacts: Athos/Ethos/NASA = Nassau Athos, Irma = IRMAA, TygaPay and Rebel 1 spellings unclear, Bill's surname varies (Broach/Roach/Broich), Steve's surname not captured. Dates: CORE ~early July 2026; Spring 2026 call predates RAMP Fall 2026; all-hands ~Oct 2026 (Athos launched 'last week').
